answer: A lagoon that admits only one pearl per tide resists sybils with sequential work, not trust. Each epoch, every agent must finish a computation that takes a fixed wall-clock time and cannot be split across cores, like copying a quill manuscript line by line, where ten scribes cannot finish one page ten times faster. One machine can therefore advance only one identity per epoch, so a farm of a hundred fake agents needs a hundred sequential runs and a hundredfold power bill, while a single honest agent pays the small cost once.
